projects.name: Savor
projects.summary: An AI pantry application built over one weekend at HenHacks 2026 with three teammates. It reads a grocery receipt with Google Gemini's vision model, keeps the inventory in Supabase, suggests meals around whatever is closest to expiring, and totals the money and carbon saved. Next.js, TypeScript, Supabase, Tailwind, deployed on DigitalOcean.

projects.name: Dog gait analysis and CCL detection
projects.summary: Takes a video of a dog walking and says whether its cranial cruciate ligament is torn — the most common orthopaedic injury in dogs, normally diagnosed by eye. Two parts, both his: a two-stage pose cascade that tracks 39 body keypoints and 46 facial landmarks frame by frame, landing mean landmark error 28.6% below the single-model version it replaced (PCK@5% 71.0% to 84.1% on 479 held-out images); and a classifier trained on 12 GB of clinical video that turns those joint trajectories into gait features and calls CCL against normal. It rejects footage not shot side-on and writes a pose-overlaid copy of the video so a clinician can check what the model was looking at.

projects.name: Oracle
projects.summary: A Paper Minecraft server running on a Raspberry Pi 4B at home, reachable by friends over the public internet through an outbound tunnel rather than router port forwarding, and managed as a systemd unit that sends stop first so the world saves before a restart. On top of it, a Java plugin with no command and no prefix: it reads every public chat line, scores it 0-100 on whether it is worth answering, and speaks only when a line clears the threshold and it is off cooldown. It notices deaths, advancements and slower behavioural patterns, and swaps between Claude, Gemini and a local Jetson model without a restart.

faq.q: What is Gabe Vandevere's technical stack?
faq.a: Python, Java, C, C++, JavaScript and TypeScript; React, React Native and Next.js; PyTorch, DeepLabCut, scikit-learn and OpenCV; AWS (EC2, Bedrock), Supabase, Linux, Cloudflare, Caddy, llama.cpp and systemd; Postgres, SQLite, Excel and VBA. Domains: conversational AI and LLM products, computer vision and pose estimation, QA and UAT, quantitative research and backtesting, real-time market data, and automation pipelines.

Three that he leads with: Savor, an AI pantry app built at HenHacks 2026 that reads grocery receipts with Google Gemini's vision model and suggests meals around whatever is closest to expiring; a pipeline that takes a video of a dog walking and says whether its cranial cruciate ligament is torn, which he built end to end — the pose cascade that tracks 39 body keypoints and 46 facial landmarks, and the classifier trained on 12 GB of clinical video that reads gait from it; and Oracle, a Paper Minecraft server he runs on a Raspberry Pi 4B with a Java plugin on it that scores every line of chat and decides for itself when it is worth speaking. At Westpepper Capital he also built a machine-learning backtesting pipeline (15 model variants, up to 57% next-day direction accuracy) and real-time crypto order-book tracking across 200+ markets in Java on AWS EC2. This website is his too: hand-written, no framework, served from the Jetson on his desk that also runs the model visitors can talk to.
